page: Microsoft Azure D128s_v7 is a general-purpose server belonging to the Dsv7 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration features 128 dedicated vCPUs derived from 64 physical cores with Hyper-Threading enabled, providing 2.0 threads per core. The system includes 512.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is also top-tier, with both small-block cached and large-block uncached read operations reaching the top 10% threshold. Single-core performance is moderate, placing in the middle 50% for stress-ng single-core tests. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, which contribute to strong performance in cryptography, compression, and medium-model LLM inference prompt processing.

Given its high resource density and dedicated CPU allocation, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads that can leverage its 128 vCPUs without requiring local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. It is configured for large-scale database operations, static web serving, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
